_note: Registry of third-party animation engines this skill can route to. Nothing here is vendored: `node engines.mjs install <name>` does a shallow git clone into ./engines/<name> and records the commit. Licenses were read from each repo's LICENSE file on 2026-11-12; re-check before redistributing.

ui-cards.title: Clean UI cards (built in)
ui-cards.best_for: System design, tech and product explainers, Figma-tutorial look, Hindi voice + Hinglish captions

anidoodle.title: anidoodle (alexgreensh)
anidoodle.best_for: Hand-drawn / painted illustration, loops, stickers, storybook and 3D motion graphics in 32 art styles; deterministic code art; scored films
warnings: Optional sound pack is ~373 MB; never download without asking the user
Narration providers send text to a third-party voice service (we use our own Hindi TTS instead)
plugin.json, package.json and shell scripts were not audited

huashu-art-motion.title: huashu-art-motion (alchaincyf)
huashu-art-motion.license: MIT (with exceptions for some fonts and character art, see repo README)
huashu-art-motion.best_for: Art-history and era styles (Van Gogh, ink wash, ukiyo-e-like, pop art...) and 9 explainer narration grammars (Kurzgesagt, Vox, whiteboard, kinetic type, 3Blue1Brown, keynote, finance chart)
warnings: Do not enable its voice cloning (calls a third-party API); we use our own TTS
Its version check runs git ls-remote and writes .last-update-check in its folder
Its agent is told to write lessons back into its own reference files; review those diffs
Character artwork and Clawd are not MIT; do not reuse them
No Windows setup guide; Python tooling untested here

claude-animation-base.title: ClaudeAnimationBase (JohnHeibel)
claude-animation-base.best_for: Hand-painted 2D cartoon (p5.js + p5.brush), painted characters with acted emotions, no on-screen text; storyboard-first process
warnings: Its mascot character (Clawd) is Anthropic's; use the engine and guide, not the character, in public work
Render launches Chrome with --allow-file-access-from-files and loads a Google Fonts stylesheet
src/ was not audited

manim.title: Manim best practices + composer (adithya-s-k)
manim.license: MIT (covers the repo's notes/examples, not Manim itself)
manim.best_for: Math, algorithms, graphs, data-structure and ML visuals in 3Blue1Brown style (Python Manim Community)
needs: Cairo/Pango (manimpango) on Windows can be painful
warnings: Python was NOT installed on the machine this skill was built on; Manim output was never rendered here
Notes on 9:16 are from general Manim knowledge, not the repo; verify with `manim cfg show`

lemo-opuscar.title: lemo-opuscar (LemoLab)
lemo-opuscar.best_for: 66 film styles incl. paper-lantern, white-model, spy-titles, ink-wash, shadow-puppet, microscope, ascii-crt, engraving, archive-lighttable, art-deco; deterministic canvas/three.js/WebGL renders
needs: Git Bash or WSL on Windows
warnings: setup.sh hard-resets its clone to main on every run and downloads npm/pip/Chromium/model/sample packs: do not run it blindly
Its agent installs per-style packages and may fetch voices, data and fonts from the network at render time
.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugin hooks, core/ and tools/ were not audited
Use its style specs, not its demo stories; do not use its narration or sample libraries (we use our own Hindi voice and mix)

bang-motion.title: Bang Motion (bangtutorial)
bang-motion.best_for: Browser motion graphics as one index.html: 10 style directions, 19 opener concepts, 6 explainer styles with starters (16:9 or 9:16); strong anti-slide rules (continuous motion, deterministic timeline)
warnings: Its docs are written in Indonesian
Its own scripts (export-frames, snap) were read but not run
Use its style/structure specs; we keep our own Hindi/English voice, music and mix and mux over its silent render

vox-explainer.title: Vox explainer (CK42BB)
vox-explainer.best_for: The Vox look (editorial paper collage) and the Vox narrative arc / beat budgeting
warnings: Its pipeline calls the paid Atlas Cloud API (image, video, voice, music models) with an API key: NOT used here. Only its writing arc and visual grammar are adopted
Ask before any third-party generation API is used

claude-drawing.title: Claude Drawing (cloveric)
claude-drawing.best_for: 83 procedural painting styles drawn with code (numpy + Pillow, no image model), draw-on GIFs: ink wash, watercolour, oil impasto, ukiyo-e, clay, cyanotype, stained glass, isometric, synthwave ...
warnings: Python is not installed on this machine, so these styles are blocked until it is
Upstream SKILL.md is ~740 KB and was not vendored; only README + docs/ are
Its image output is stills/GIFs: animate by sequencing draw-on frames, then mux our voice over

earshot.title: earshot (Leonxlnx): ears for coding agents
earshot.best_for: Lets the agent HEAR: describe a sound, score it against a description, rank candidate downloads, find moments, check sync of sound to picture cuts, measure loudness/tempo/key, detect code-synthesized vs real recordings, critique a film soundtrack; also a bank of 252 synthesized sounds
needs: ~1.1 GB of two open models (CLAP, AST) downloaded on first use
warnings: Not installed here. Installing downloads ~1.1 GB: ask the user first
Each CLI call loads the models (20-40 s); use its MCP server for many calls
It cannot judge taste, emotion, licences or speech content; hints only for events inside a busy mix
Optional paths (llm critique) send audio to Gemini with the user own key: never use without explicit consent

real-sfx.title: Real SFX (Clipwing/skills) - link only
real-sfx.license: NONE DECLARED (repo has no LICENSE file): do not copy or vendor
real-sfx.best_for: Sound-designing a finished motion video with real recorded effects from the user own library, placed on the exact frame, with a verify/critique loop
needs: a sound library the user owns
warnings: Not vendored: no licence. Use it only if the user installs it themselves
Reelsmith implements the same idea natively for our pipeline: sfx.mjs + cue-timed files in audio.mjs

openverse.title: Openverse API (built in as scripts/sfx.mjs)
openverse.license: service; every sound carries its own Creative Commons licence
openverse.best_for: Finding CC0 / public-domain / CC BY sound effects (mostly Freesound) without an API key
warnings: Anonymous use only (page size 20); licence data may be incomplete: verify the landing page
Downloads need the user OK; CC BY needs credits in the post; never NC/ND
